- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to recent highs.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -1.0) — add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion or panic-driven dips.
- Overshoot after sharp spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days) — apply a 10–15% downward correction to prevent overreaction.
- Lagged forecasts (especially 10+ days ahead) consistently overpredict — apply a 1–3% decay factor per day to reduce forward bias.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, reduce forecast slope — avoid steep declines unless sentiment confirms bearish reversal.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show price drop > 2%, adjust forecast to align with 20-day moving average or 10-day SMA.
- Avoid forecasting “new highs” when sentiment is weak — cap forecast at 1.5x recent 10-day high unless sentiment > 1.2.
